subject: Token emission degradation — streaming chat (prod)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@harborpay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:12:43 -0700
Subject: Token emission slowdown observed in prod (streaming API)

Mina / Ben,

We're seeing a noticeable slow-down in streamed responses from Redwood's streaming endpoint starting ~07:55 PDT. The chat UI at HarborPay is receiving chunks much less frequently — responses arrive in fewer, larger chunks and time-to-first-byte (TTFB) has increased from ~120ms to ~800ms on average. This began right after today's 07:45 deploy window.

Impact:
- ~18% of sessions report UI stalls (users see typing indicator freeze)
- Spike in perceived latency during payment confirmation flows

I attached a representative trace. Please advise immediate mitigations — our SREs asked if there's a temporary config we can flip to reduce customer-visible impact while you investigate.

Thanks,
Samir
Product Ops — HarborPay
[Attachment: chat_trace_20261005.log (text)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@harborpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:28:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token emission slowdown observed in prod (streaming API)

Samir — thanks for the signal and the trace. We're looking into it now. Initial notes:

- We saw a deployment at 07:43 that changed batching/window heuristics for long-sequence generation; engineering is rolling back that change to verify.
- Short-term mitigations you can apply while we validate rollback:
  * Switch calls to non-streaming (one-shot) generation for critical flows — this avoids token-by-token emission variability.
  * Reduce max_tokens and lowering `stream_chunk_size` on your client (we can suggest exact values).
  * If possible, enable client-side buffering with minimal typing indicator (show immediate partial responses while continuing to stream behind the scenes).

Can you confirm whether you can accept non-streaming for the payment-confirmation flow for the next 2–4 hours? We can also open a temporary routing rule to send HarborPay calls to a stable fleet in a different region.

I'm including Ben and Laura — Ben will lead the rollback/triage, Laura will coordinate credits and SLA communications.

Mina
Support Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@harborpay.com>, Lynn Gomez <lynn.gomez@harborpay.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:12:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token emission slowdown observed in prod (streaming API)

Team — quick technical update from triage:

- Root cause (prelim): an aggressive change in the runtime's continuous-batching window made the system wait up to 600ms for additional tokens before flushing chunks for certain model sequence shapes. That reduced throughput variability for most workloads but caused starvation for short-turnaround chat sessions.
- Action taken: rolled back the batching-window change at 09:58; routing-flags flipped to route HarborPay to the stable fleet at 10:05.
- Immediate mitigation we recommend on your side (HarborPay):
  1) Use non-streaming for the payment-confirm endpoint until we confirm steady-state (expected 2–6 hours).
  2) If non-streaming is not acceptable, add client-side prefetch of up to 16 tokens to avoid UI stalls.

We've also pushed a diagnostic build that enables more granular stream-flush telemetry for a 1-hr window; asking HarborPay to keep trace capture on for the next hour.

Next: we'll share a draft postmortem and a timeline once we validate the rollback metrics. Laura — can you prepare the credit estimate and coordinate the official notification?

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: HB-4721 — Post-incident follow-up and remediation summary

Samir / Lynn —

Thank you for collaborating closely during the incident. Below is the summary and our next steps. I'm attaching a draft postmortem for your review.

Incident summary:
- Window: 2026-10-05 07:55 — 2026-10-05 10:20 PDT (root-cause window; rollback at 09:58, traffic fully normalized by 10:20).
- Symptom: delayed token emission (chunking starvation) leading to elevated TTFB and perceived UI stalls.
- Root cause: an intended optimization to the continuous-batching window that introduced an unintended 400–600ms buffering delay for short conversations.

Customer-impact mitigation we executed:
- Rolled back the batching change at 09:58.
- Temporarily routed HarborPay to our stable fleet and recommended non-streaming for critical endpoints while we validated metrics.
- Enabled enhanced stream telemetry to confirm flush latency improvements.

Compensation and next steps:
- We're preparing a one-time account credit to HarborPay for the impacted window; Laura will follow up with the amount and timing.
- Engineering plans: a safer rollout path for batching heuristics (canary per-customer flags, automated rollback on flush-latency regressions) and a follow-up patch with additional unit tests.
- We welcome HarborPay's review of the attached draft postmortem; please flag any missing details or corrections.

Attachments: HB-4721-postmortem-draft.pdf, support_manifest_20261006.pdf

Sincerely,
Mina Haddad
Support Lead — Redwood Inference
